name: canonical-edge-case-matrix-v0
description: A manifest-driven edge-case matrix for current LUASCRIPT language/runtime features. This scoped matrix classifies representative cases without promoting broad language support.

cases.claim: Simple numeric/string values preserve runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
Boolean negation and null-equivalent emission remain explicit across current emitted targets.
The current plain-template-literal foothold preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
A small arithmetic-precedence expression preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
cases.source:
let value = 2 + 3 * 4 - 5;
console.log("edge_value_precedence", value);

cases.claim: A small while loop with break and continue preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
A narrow numeric for loop preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
Return-only branch classification preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
A small short-circuiting expression with skipped side effects preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
A narrow closure-mutation pattern preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
A small local-shadowing pattern preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
A small recursive function preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
The Python V1.3 bounded sequence-slice foothold preserves string/list slice stdout across current emitted targets.
cases.source:
word = "LuaScript"
numbers = [2, 4, 6, 8, 10]
part = word[1:4]
mid = numbers[1:4]
print("edge_data", part, len(mid), mid[0], mid[2])

cases.claim: A small JavaScript array/object mutation pattern preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
The current Python list mutation and membership foothold preserves runtime stdout across current emitted JavaScript and Python targets.
cases.source:
items = [2, 3]
items.append(4)
last = items.pop()
items.append(last + 1)
print("edge_data_py_list", len(items), items[0], items[2], 3 in items)

cases.claim: The current .ls portable-semantics profile preserves length, slice, index, and mutation stdout across current emitted targets.
Runtime errors remain observable target-runtime failures rather than silently passing.
cases.source: console.log("edge_error", missing_call());

cases.claim: A Python undefined-call pattern remains an observable runtime failure in current Python and JavaScript targets.
cases.source: print("edge_error_py", missing_call())

cases.claim: A Python out-of-range list index remains an observable runtime failure in the current Python target.
cases.source:
items = [1]
print("edge_error_index", items[2])

cases.feature: Lua one-based table index to zero-based targets
cases.claim: Lua one-based table indexes repair to zero-based JavaScript, Python, and emitted .ls targets for the named V2.1 slice.
The current Python negative-step range foothold preserves runtime stdout across current emitted targets.
cases.source:
total = 0
for value in range(5, -1, -2):
    total = total + value
print("edge_target_py_range", total)

cases.claim: The current .ls portable-semantics profile repairs JS-like truthiness across current emitted targets.
Unsupported slice-step syntax remains fail-closed with an explicit diagnostic.
cases.source:
word = "LuaScript"
print(word[0:6:2])
cases.expectedDiagnosticPattern: Unsupported Python input feature: slice steps

cases.claim: Unsupported JavaScript for-of syntax remains fail-closed with an explicit diagnostic.
cases.expectedDiagnosticPattern: Unsupported JavaScript control flow: for-of loops

cases.claim: Unsupported JavaScript try/catch/finally syntax remains fail-closed with an explicit diagnostic.
Unsupported JavaScript object spread remains fail-closed with an explicit diagnostic.
